Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no commas after 'Veni' in the first two strophes and prints 'sancte' lower-case; the 1962 sets them and capitalises; 1862 'coelitus' for the 1962 'caelitus'; 1862 'solatium' for the 1962 'solacium'; 1862 'Alleluja' for the 1962 'Alleluia'. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 46797-46824, which prints 'aridum' at 46817 and 'Flecte' at 46818, and 'in fletu folatium' at 46812. Recorded limitation: LETTERFORMS INFERRED. The 1862 layer reads 'toridum' at 45905 for 'aridum' and 'Y \ecte' at 45908 for 'Flecte'; the 1570 supplies both at the same place. The 1862 also drops the ornamental V ('VEni'). The solatium/solacium split is a t/c orthographic variant, not a different word, and the 1862 and the 1570 agree against the 1962 on it.

propers.name: Sequence
propers.text:
Veni, Sancte Spiritus, et emitte caelitus lucis tuae radium. Veni, pater
pauperum, veni, dator munerum, veni, lumen cordium. Consolator optime,
dulcis hospes animae, dulce refrigerium. In labore requies, in aestu
temperies, in fletu solacium. O lux beatissima, reple cordis intima tuorum
fidelium. Sine tuo numine, nihil est in homine, nihil est innoxium. Lava
quod est sordidum, riga quod est aridum, sana quod est saucium. Flecte quod
est rigidum, fove quod est frigidum, rege quod est devium. Da tuis
fidelibus, in te confidentibus, sacrum septenarium. Da virtutis meritum, da
salutis exitum, da perenne gaudium. Amen. Alleluia.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

Read at printed pp. 234-236 = leaves n271-n273, under `Sequence, Whit-Sunday.` and the incipit `Veni Sancte Spiritus.` Ten stanzas against the Missal's ten strophes, one for one. The Missal's closing `Amen. Alleluja.` is not rendered.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 4 tokens differ only in accent, ligature or orthography as the 1862 text layer renders them (D6mine,/Domine,; sanctum/Sanctum; D6minum./Dominum; ejusdem/ejusdem.); 1862 text layer reads 'QAcrificia,' where the 1962 prints 'Sacrificia,'; 1862 text layer reads 'ta' where the 1962 prints 'oblata'; 1862 text layer reads 'consp6ctibus,' where the 1962 prints 'conspectibus,'; 1862 text layer reads 'absfimat,' where the 1962 prints 'absumat,'; 1862 text layer reads 'discipu16rum' where the 1962 prints 'discipulorum'; 1862 text layer reads 'efimdem' where the 1962 prints 'eundem'; 1862 text layer reads 'unit' where the 1962 prints 'unitate'; 1862 text layer emits 3 stray fragment(s) at line breaks ('ob0', 'l', 'te'); the word 'nostrum' the 1962 prints is not matched in the 1862 span. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 410 (artifact PDF p. 524), text layer, lines 38875-38884: 24 of 25 tokens match exactly or in orthography, 0 word-level difference(s). Recorded limitation: CONFIDENCE MEDIUM, AND THE REASON IS AN INFERENCE RATHER THAN A READING. At this locus the alignment leaves more than one token unread in one of the two witnesses - the differences below name them - so at least one word's letterforms were inferred from the other witness instead of being read in both. The prayer as a whole is corroborated; the individual word is not. This repository holds no page image of the 1862 for the temporal run, so the inference cannot be closed here; the 1922 Mame's pages do render, and opening the Mame page named under corroboration would settle it. Verdict settled by hand: the two 1862 word-level differences are recogniser artifacts - one word broken across a line, and the older spelling 'eumdem' for 'eundem' in the conclusion - and the 1922 Mame carries the prayer with none. Antecedent read on the 1862 text layer alone; this repository holds no page image of that book for the temporal run. Alignment over the aligned span: 14 of 26 antecedent-covered tokens exact, 9 differing only in orthography or accent as the layer renders them, 2 word-level difference(s), 0 1962 token(s) beyond the aligned span. The 1922 Tours Mame, an independent public-domain witness, carries the same prayer with 0 word-level difference(s).

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Sumpsimus, Domine, sacri dona mysterii: humiliter deprecantes; ut, quae in
tui commemorationem nos facere praecepisti, in nostrae proficiant
infirmitatis auxilium: Qui vivis et regnas.
